text:
alex: Heads up, I tried the JS SDK quickstart in Deno and Bun for a partner demo and ran into a few runtime incompatibilities.
priya: what happened exactly?
alex: In Deno the import fails with a resolve error referencing package.json exports. In Bun some requests crash during auth because crypto.subtle isn't present in older bun builds.
maria: that's been popping up. Deno wants explicit ESM entrypoints (or a deno export) and Bun's ESM/CJS interop differs from Node.
leo: can you paste the error?
alex: Error from deno: "Uncaught Error: package.json exports do not contain ./deno". TS also warns: "Module has no default export" when using `import Redwood from 'redwood'`.
priya: I think the README examples show `import Redwood from 'redwood'` which is Node-centric. We should add runtime-specific examples and a deno-friendly entry.
maria: Agreed. Suggestion: add an explicit export like "./deno": "./dist/deno/index.mjs" and a small runtime-adapters module that detects Deno/Bun/Node and exposes adapters (fetch wrapper, crypto.subtle fallback, stream normalizer).
leo: for crypto, a tiny polyfill that calls `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` or falls back to `await import('jose')`-style helper would work. Keep it optional so tree-shaking removes it for Node consumers.
priya: typings: Deno consumers tend to prefer a published .d.ts alongside the deno entry. We should add `dist/deno/index.d.ts` and include an export so TypeScript in Deno finds it.
alex: Bun quirk: response.body stream shape differs and our parseBody util threw on `instanceof ReadableStream`. Quick patch: prefer `response.arrayBuffer()` then parse from that as the fallback.
maria: Also consider adding `redwood/deno` examples under examples/deno-quickstart with a deno.json and import_map.json so partners can run them with one command. Example snippet in README: ```ts
import { Redwood } from 'redwood/deno';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY')! });
```
leo: For package.json exports, we can do conditional exports covering browser/node/deno: ```json
{"exports": {"./deno": "./dist/deno/index.mjs","./browser": "./dist/web/index.mjs",".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs","require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"}}}
```
priya: CI: add a matrix job to run the JS SDK samples on node 18/20, deno 1.34+/1.35+, bun nightly. We'll catch regressions early.
ci-bot: nightly pipeline failed - deno sample import error: https://ci.internal/redwood/deno-quickstart/789 (logs attached)
alex: I'll open a PR to add the deno export and the example quickstart. Will include a tiny test that runs `deno run --quiet --allow-net examples/deno-quickstart/main.ts`.
maria: I'll take the runtime-adapters + auth fallback (crypto.subtle shim) and add unit tests that simulate Bun missing subtle.
leo: I'll own the package.json exports + types publishing changes and add a short compatibility table to the SDK README listing exact runtime versions we support.
priya: perfect. Also add a troubleshooting note about import maps and when to use `import { Redwood } from 'redwood/deno'` vs `redwood` default import.
ci-bot: Created issue #512: "SDK: Deno/Bun runtime compatibility - deno export, runtime adapters, crypto fallback, fetch normalization" assigned to alex,maria,leo.
alex: thanks. PR incoming within the day. We'll avoid pushing Node-only examples into quickstarts from now on.
priya: :thumbsup: this should reduce onboarding friction for partners using edge runtimes.
